messages:
elena: Heads-up — we just opened initial Dedicated mi500 pools in APAC (ap-sg) and EU (eu-frankfurt). This is an early-availability wave for customers who need a mid/high-throughput option between A100x and MI300. Docs + opt-in link: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/mi500-availability :tada:

deploy-bot: rollout started -> ap-sg-1, eu-frankfurt-1 (canaries live). Tracking job ID: rbw-roll-2112345678. Logs: /deploys/rbw-roll-2112345678

raj: Nice — for customers on existing Dedicated contracts, can they map commit hours to mi500 or is this separate SKU?

elena: Good q. Existing Reserved Capacity can be migrated to mi500 only via a formal change order (sales+rev signoff). We built a migration flag but it requires SLA acceptance. I'll loop in sales ops for customer-specific mapping.

mira: What should SRE watch for on the canaries? Any new signals or failure modes?

elena: Primary: p95 latency, token throughput, and memory OOMs. mi500 has different perf characteristics at long sequence lengths — watch tail latency for >2k tokens. Sample metric queries: `sum(rate(tokens_served[5m])) by (pool)`, `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le,pool))`

andrew: Billing SKU? Need to update monthly chargeback report.

elena: New SKU: `dedicated.mi500.hour`. Billing goes live for new reservations starting 2026-04-01. Existing commitments moved via change order will keep original pricing until their term ends.

ops-bot: Notifying customers with active Dedicated credits and contacts in the next hour. Email template: /templates/mi500_early_access.md

sarah: Runtime question — do we need new kernel bundles or is this a drop-in?

elena: Runtime supports mi500 with the current compiler pipeline but you must enable the MI500 microkernel set (`--enable-mi500-kernels`) in runtime configs. Most common quant/kv-cache paths are supported; we have a small set of fallback kernels for edge cases.

raj: Any guidance for customers on model choices?

elena: Recommendation: mi500 excels for 8k-32k context on medium-sized dense models (20B–70B). We'll publish perf profiles tomorrow. Early tip: prefer int4/ q4f15 quant for best cost/lateny tradeoff.

elena: How to opt in (self-serve):
```
# reserve via CLI (example)
redwood reserve --pool mi500 --region ap-sg --commit 3mo --gpus 4 --contact sales@redwood.ai
```

elena: Known limitations: no TPU-style SPMD sharding yet; some tiny fp16 kernels will be slower than on MI300 for very large dense models. We'll annotate these in the perf doc.

mira: Thanks — SRE will add p95 alert + token rate dashboard.

andrew: Will update billing codes and tell finance ops.

elena: Follow-up: Docs will include migration playbook, offer migration review for top 10 customers, and an FAQ. I'll post the perf readout + sample workloads tomorrow. :rocket:
